paper.title: Deep Learning for ECG Analysis: Benchmarks and Insights from PTB-XL

project.title: Can a Small Model Tell a Normal Heartbeat from an Abnormal One?
project.question: Using the public PTB-XL ECG dataset, how well does a small convolutional network separate normal from abnormal ECGs compared with a simple feature-based baseline, and which abnormal classes are hardest?
project.hypothesis: A small 1D CNN trained on the 100 Hz recordings will score higher ROC-AUC than logistic regression on hand-made features, and errors will concentrate in classes with subtle waveform changes.
data: PTB-XL v1.0.3 from PhysioNet (CC BY 4.0), 100 Hz records
risks: Downloading the full dataset is slow on some connections; start with the 100 Hz records only.
Training a CNN on a CPU can be slow; use a free Colab runtime or fewer leads.
This is a learning project, not a medical device: results must not be used to diagnose anyone.

quiz.question: You load the PTB-XL metadata with pandas. Which call shows the first five rows?
Which expression keeps only the rows whose fold number is at most 8?
A 10-second ECG lead recorded at 100 Hz contains how many samples?
Why might you prefer the 100 Hz version of PTB-XL for a laptop project?
options: Fewer samples per record means less memory and faster training

quiz.question: What does ROC-AUC measure?
options: How many features the model uses
The percentage of correct labels at one threshold
How well the model's scores rank positive cases above negative ones across all thresholds

quiz.question: A model that assigns random scores would have an ROC-AUC close to which value?
Why does PTB-XL put all ECGs from one patient in the same fold?
options: To make the folds equal in size
So the model is not tested on a patient it already saw in training

quiz.question: When should you use the test fold?
options: Once, at the end, after all choices were made on the validation fold

guides.why: Load the metadata table and the signal files.
guides.summary: pandas stores tables as DataFrames. You can read a CSV file, look at a few rows, select columns and keep only the rows that meet a condition. For PTB-XL, the metadata table lists one ECG per row with its labels and fold number.
steps: Read a CSV file into a DataFrame
Select columns and filter rows with a condition
guides.practice: Load any small CSV file and count how many rows have each value in one column.

guides.why: An ECG is a time series; 100 Hz means 100 samples per second per lead.
guides.summary: A signal is a value measured over time. The sampling rate says how many measurements are taken each second. An ECG lead at 100 Hz has 100 values for every second, and plotting them against time shows the heartbeat shape.
steps: Learn what a time series is
Understand sampling rate and its unit (Hz)
Plot one lead and identify heartbeats
guides.practice: Make a sine wave with numpy at two sampling rates and plot both to see the difference.

guides.why: The paper compares models with ROC-AUC, so you will too.
guides.summary: Binary classification sorts items into two groups. Many models output a score, and a threshold turns it into a label. The ROC curve shows the trade-off between catching positives and raising false alarms at every threshold, and the area under it summarizes ranking quality.
steps: See how a threshold turns scores into labels
Draw an ROC curve from scores
Compute the area under the curve with scikit-learn
guides.practice: Invent ten scores and labels by hand, sort them, and sketch the ROC curve on paper.

guides.why: PTB-XL keeps each patient in one fold; mixing them would inflate your score.
guides.summary: Models are trained on one part of the data, tuned on another and tested on a third. Leakage happens when information from the evaluation data reaches training, making results look better than they are. Keeping each patient in a single fold is one way PTB-XL prevents it.
steps: Learn why three splits are used
Find the fold column and the recommended split
List common leakage sources such as scaling on all data
Check that no patient appears in two splits
guides.practice: Write down three ways leakage could happen in an ECG project and how you would check each one.
